history.summary: THIS IS A JAIN (DIGAMBARA) TEMPLE, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. The Dimapur Jain Temple on Jain Temple Road was built in 1947 by eight Sethi families of the Digambara sect, the first non-Naga settlers of Nagaland; they had earlier built the first Jain temple in Kohima in 1920 and moved to Dimapur in 1944 during the Japanese invasion of World War II. Lord Mahavira is the Moolnayak (primary deity); the back portion housing idols of Adinath, Bahubali and Bharat Swami was added in 1989 (Panch Kalyanak by Ganini Shri Suparshmati Mataji). The temple is managed by the SD Jain Samaj Dimapur. COORD CONFLICT: Wikipedia gives rounded coordinates 25.92 N, 93.73 E; the map-listing pin is 25.9059 N, 93.7252 E - both marked approximate.

name: Dimapur Jain Temple
town_description: Dimapur is Nagaland's largest city and its commercial hub, and the main gateway into the state. It sits at the foothills of the Naga Hills in Dimapur district and is home to the state's only civil airport and a key railway station. The town is known for the medieval Kachari Rajbari ruins and its mix of Naga and non-Naga communities.

travel.road: On Jain Temple Road, Marwari Patti / West Yard Colony area; auto-rickshaws from the city centre
